title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 3: Augustine In Joh. 86 — praescientia pleaded against grace
pass_a_gloss: Most excellently Augustine, on John, tractate 86: They defend the foreknowledge of God against the grace of God, who say we were elected before the foundation of the world because God foresaw that we would be good. For they were not elected because they were good, who would not have been good unless they had been elected. Why then should not we also say that they defend the foreknowledge of God against the grace of God, who say we were elected because God foresaw us as loving him? since assuredly we should never be lovers of God unless we had been elected.
pass_b_english: Augustine (In John, tract. 86) puts it best: they defend God's foreknowledge against his grace when they say we were elect before the world's foundation because God foresaw we would be good. They were not elect because they were good — they would not have been good unless elect. So we may say the same of those who claim we were elect because God foresaw us as loving him: we would never love God unless we had been elect.
source_text: Optime Augustinus, in Johan. tract. 86. Praescientiam Dei defendunt contra gratiam Dei, qui dicunt nos electos ante mundi constitutionem quia praescivit nos Deus futuros bonos. Non enim electi sunt quia boni fuerunt, qui boni non essent nisi electi essent. Quidni igitur & nos dicamus, eos praescientiam Dei defendere contra gratiam Dei, qui dicunt nos electos, quia Deus praescivit nos ut illum diligentes? cum utique Dei amantes nunquam essemus nisi electi fuissemus.
